parsed_output.hypothesis_statement: Whether contracting authorities publishing CONTRACT_NOTICE and CONTRACT_AWARD_NOTICE records under CPV class 9261 constitute a stable, addressable class of actors for whom a notice-tracking or notice-value-comparison offering could be tested, given only that such notices exist and their published TOTAL_VALUE figures vary; this does not establish any need, budget for software, willingness to pay, or dissatisfaction with existing tools.

parsed_output.evidence_bound_reasoning_summary: The packet contains six rows, all from ted-eu's notices/eforms-contract-and-award resource, describing bounded sets of CONTRACT_NOTICE and CONTRACT_AWARD_NOTICE records classified under CPV class 9261. The statements establish that such notices exist (contracting authorities publish them, evidencing BUYER_OR_BUDGET_EXISTENCE), that published TOTAL_VALUE figures at notice scope differ across notices within these bounded sets (ECONOMIC_VALUE), and that this activity occurred within a defined classification (MARKET_ACTIVITY). Per eForms BT-161, TOTAL_VALUE includes options and renewals and is not realised expenditure or a price. No statement addresses recurrence of any underlying need, dissatisfaction with any current solution, gaps in existing supply, who else serves this space, distribution channels, regulatory drivers, feasibility of building anything, or willingness to pay for a product. The narrowest defensible hypothesis is that a class of contracting authorities publishing notices under this CPV code exists and is worth investigating further as a possible actor class, not that any need, budget, or demand for a specific intervention has been shown.
critical_uncertainties: Whether any contracting authority in this CPV class experiences a recurring problem, as opposed to a single observed instance of notice publication.
